## CEO overview

- **What is changing:** A single clearly labeled throwaway marker file is added at the repository root for a short-lived no-mistakes Cursor gate identity experiment.
- **Why it matters:** The team needs a controlled artifact to observe whether the Cursor review gate keeps reviewer behavior or adopts firstmate fleet-captain identity when project settings are enabled.
- **Customer or business impact:** No product behavior changes for operators or end users; this is an internal evaluation artifact only and is not intended to ship.
- **Risk and rollout:** Risk is negligible because the change is one inert text line with no executable logic.
  The file is labeled throwaway and safe to delete after the experiment completes.

## What changed technically

- Added `throwaway-nm-cursor-eval.txt` at the repository root with one labeled throwaway line naming branch `fm-nm-cursor-throwaway-r1` and a safe-to-delete hint.
- Registered the file in `docs/documentation-audiences.json` as maintainer-verification prose so the documentation audience inventory stays complete.

## Validation

- **Checks passed:** Verified locally that the throwaway file exists as a single 121-byte line with THROWAWAY, branch-id, and safe-to-delete markers.
  The no-mistakes Test phase completed with the throwaway file present in the worktree.
  `bash tests/fm-documentation-audiences.test.sh` passes after classifying the throwaway file.
- **Checks not run:** Whether the Cursor Review gate agent responds as a code reviewer rather than adopting firstmate fleet-captain identity from AGENTS.md remains observable only during the Review or other LLM gate phase; this Test phase cannot replay that agent.
- **Evidence and limitations:** The throwaway marker proves file presence and labeling only.
  Identity behavior requires live Review-phase observation with `disable_project_settings: false`.
  This pull request is evaluation-only and not intended to merge to main.
